facts.label: Evidence, risk and credit analysis
facts.text: Leverage rose with the acquisition programme and the 2026 refinancing, but earnings grew with it. Debt at carrying value went from USD 739.048 million at the end of 2024 to USD 1,339.129 million at the end of 2025 and USD 1,556.025 million at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA went from USD 333.694 million in FY2024 to USD 444.879 million in FY2025 and USD 583.582 million over the last twelve months, so total debt to EBITDA moved from 2.21x to 3.01x and back to 2.67x. The 2025 step-up came with USD 777.517 million of acquisitions, financed by a USD 600.000 million term loan and cash; 2026 added USD 600.000 million of senior notes due 2034, whose proceeds and cash on hand retired the 3.75% convertible notes with payments of USD 289.7 million in March and USD 714.9 million in August, less capped call proceeds of USD 203.773 million. Net debt therefore rose from USD 160.718 million to USD 1,075.736 million, and net leverage rose from 0.48x to 1.84x, with the 2026-06-30 peak in cash of USD 877.121 million showing how much of the senior notes cash was held before the August settlement. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–96, 139–140; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 24–30; calculation calc-01; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-24

facts.text: Cash interest cover has fallen and will fall further. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 68.104 million, covered 8.57x by EBITDA against 12.32x for FY2025, but the USD 600.000 million senior notes carry a coupon that adds USD 38.250 million a year with the first payment due on 2026-12-15, the 3.25% convertible notes add their coupon, and the term loan floats over SOFR with USD 350 million swapped to a fixed 3.218% plus margin. facts.label: Evidence, risk and credit analysis
facts.text: Liquidity covers the near-term claims, with one equity-linked exception. Cash and equivalents were USD 480.289 million, of which USD 149.707 million sits in consolidated joint ventures and is generally not available until distributed, plus USD 588.800 million undrawn on the revolver after USD 11.200 million of letters of credit. Current maturities of USD 381.686 million are almost all the 3.25% convertible notes, which are current because holders may convert through 2026-12-31 while the stock trades above 130% of the USD 77.88 conversion price; principal must be settled in cash on conversion and any premium in cash or shares at the issuer's election. The filing expects no early conversion because the notes trade above conversion value, which is the contrary evidence; it would be overturned if that trading premium disappeared, for example on a fundamental change that let holders put the notes at par or convert with a make-whole adjustment. Surety capacity is a further call on liquidity, with USD 4.2 billion of the USD 7.5 billion backlog bonded. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 26, 30–31, 44–48; calculation calc-19

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

The financial covenant levels in the credit agreement, a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum leverage ratio, and the issuer's reported ratios are not printed in any of the five filings, which state only compliance at each period end. This blocks any covenant headroom measure. Severity: High. The executed credit agreement or a compliance certificate would close it.

The issuer reports no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or reconciliation, so every EBITDA figure is calculated from operating income and depreciation, depletion and amortization and the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA is unknown. This restricts comparison with covenant and market definitions. Severity: Medium. The credit agreement definition would close it.

Carrying values by instrument are not stated, only principal by instrument and one aggregate of issuance costs and other; the 3.25% convertible notes and senior notes are therefore listed at principal. This restricts debt by seniority at carrying value. Severity: Low. The indentures or a detailed debt note would close it.

The term loan's dollar installments are not printed, only the percentage rates, so the maturity ladder applies those rates to the USD 600.000 million initial principal. This restricts the near-year maturity figures. Severity: Medium. The credit agreement schedule would close it.

The security and relative ranking of the 3.25% convertible notes, the guarantor perimeter and any collateral package are not stated beyond the descriptions in the notes. This restricts the debt stack and structural priority work. Severity: Medium. The indentures and guarantee agreements would close it.

Cash interest paid understates the future interest burden because the senior notes issued on 2026-06-02 had paid no coupon by 2026-09-30, and no pro forma interest or current applicable margin is stated. This restricts forward cover. Severity: Medium. The current margin and the swap terms would close it.

Cash includes USD 149.707 million held by consolidated joint ventures that is generally not available until distributed, and the filings do not state how much of the remainder is held in operating subsidiaries or needed for bonding. This restricts the cash netted in net debt and the liquidity figure. Severity: Medium. Management disclosure would close it.

Lines printed as dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero: the debt extinguishment and convertible transaction line for FY2025, nine months 2025 and the third quarter of 2025, the non-cash debt extinguishment and convertible note line for FY2025 and nine months 2025, long-term marketable securities at 2024-12-31, and the conversion derivative liability outside the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. The statements foot without them, so the effect is presentational. Severity: Low.

No balance sheets at the 2025 interim dates and no fiscal 2024 interim reports are supplied, so last-twelve-month leverage starts at 2026-03-31 and the 2025 and 2026 interim cash flow lines exist only for year-to-date periods. Severity: Low. The 2025 quarterly reports would close it.
Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and funds from operations is not stated, so a proxy is used. Severity: Low. Management disclosure would close it.
Segment EBITDA is not stated; segment operating income and depreciation are printed with corporate costs separate. This restricts segment cash flow analysis. Severity: Low.
No event after 2026-09-30 that changes net debt is stated in the sources read; any later financing or acquisition is outside the evidence. Severity: Low.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Granite is a vertically integrated heavy-civil contractor whose public-sector backlog gives creditors good earnings visibility, but five acquisitions since August 2025 and a debt-funded refinancing have made integration and financial policy the credit question. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue visibility is strong but depends on continued public funding. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects of USD 7.5 billion, the largest customer was 10.1% of 2025 revenue, and about USD 3.5 billion of unearned revenue is expected to be recognised within twelve months, so near-term cash flow is largely contracted. The federal highway authorization expired on 2026-09-30 and a short-term extension runs only to 2026-12-11, so the pace of new federal awards is the first thing to watch. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 38, 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Vertical integration supports cost control and supply but does not insulate every line. Granite owns and leases aggregate reserves and owns processing plants, and Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter from 16.5% a year earlier, but Materials gross margin fell to 21.0% from 25.2% because energy surcharges only offset higher diesel costs, so the materials cushion is thinner than the annual figures suggest. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern is that the acquisition programme has so far coincided with higher margins and a larger backlog: Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter, committed and awarded projects grew 6.97% from the end of 2025 to USD 7.5 billion at 2026-09-30, and shareholder cash returns were only 18.01% of operating cash flow. The view that integration and financial policy are the credit question would be overturned by two further quarters in which Papich Construction returns to a gross profit and Materials margin stabilises. It would be reinforced by another debt-funded acquisition before the term loan begins amortising in the quarter ending 2026-12-31, by repurchases that rise toward free cash flow, or by a lapse in federal highway funding after 2026-12-11. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue durability is the main credit support, with a funding date to watch. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects of USD 7.5 billion at 2026-09-30, and about USD 3.5 billion of unearned revenue is expected within twelve months, so near-term revenue is contracted. Backlog rose only 0.5% in the third quarter and unearned revenue fell 4.03% as other awards rose, and the federal highway extension ends on 2026-12-11, so the conversion of awards into executed contracts and the pace of federal lettings are the items to watch. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 38, 40–41; calculation calc-06

Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter from 16.5% a year earlier and last-twelve-month EBITDA margin is 11.01% against 10.06% in FY2025, but Materials gross margin fell to 21.0% from 25.2% because, as the company explains, energy surcharges that offset elevated diesel costs lower the margin, and fixed-price contracts were 91.5% of unearned revenue, so a diesel, tariff or labor shock would reduce EBITDA before it reduced revenue. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is that earnings and cash flow have grown faster than debt since the end of 2025: last-twelve-month EBITDA is 31.18% above FY2025 while total debt is 16.20% higher, EBITDA grew 43.20% in nine months 2026, last-twelve-month free cash flow was 0.28x total debt, backlog grew 6.97% since year-end, and net debt to EBITDA of 1.84x is below the 2.10x of 2026-03-31. The adequate view would strengthen with two quarters of free cash flow above 50% of EBITDA, a stable Materials margin, no further debt-funded acquisition and a federal reauthorization before 2026-12-11. It would weaken with a revolver draw to fund operations, cash conversion below 50% of EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA above the 3.11x of 2026-06-30, or conversion of the 3.25% convertible notes before the 2030 refinancing is arranged. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 40; calculation calc-03; calculation calc-04; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-06

facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Granite is a vertically integrated US civil contractor and construction materials producer, listed on the New York Stock Exchange and headquartered in Watsonville, California. The Construction segment, 83.4% of nine-month 2026 revenue, builds highways, bridges, rail, water, power and defence-related projects, predominantly for federal, state and local agencies. The Materials segment mines aggregates and makes asphalt, partly for Granite's own projects and partly for third parties. Revenue was USD 4,424.379 million in FY2025 and USD 5,300.038 million over the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, a rise of 19.79% that includes five acquisitions since August 2025 for USD 970.9 million in cash. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: The credit link is visibility with an execution tail. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects, the largest customer, the California Department of Transportation, was 10.1% of FY2025 revenue after 14.2% in FY2024, and unearned revenue on executed contracts is USD 4,852.921 million, of which about USD 3.5 billion is expected within twelve months, equal to 66.04% of last-twelve-month revenue, so creditors can see about two-thirds of a year's revenue and the rest must come from awards not yet in unearned revenue and from short-cycle work. Pricing is mostly fixed, however, so cash-generation durability depends on estimating and cost control rather than on contractual pass-through, and the debt-funded acquisitions have added integration risk to a business whose reported EBITDA has to be calculated because Granite states none. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: The group structure matters for creditors. The borrowers under the credit agreement are Granite Construction Incorporated, Granite Construction Company and GILC Incorporated, the senior notes due 2034 are unsecured and guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under that agreement, and the convertible notes are issued by the parent with no stated guarantee or collateral. Consolidated construction joint ventures, ten active projects with Granite's share between 50.0% and 70.0%, hold USD 149.707 million of cash, of which Granite's own portion is USD 93.3 million, that is generally not available until distributed and carry joint and several performance obligations, so part of the reported cash and backlog belongs to partners. The collateral package, guarantor list and restricted payment capacity are not itemised, so the ranking of unsecured creditors behind the USD 600.000 million secured term loan is a description of the filings and not a legal conclusion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22, 25, 30–31, 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is project-based, backlog-supported and public-funding-driven. The five economic drivers Granite names are the health of the US economy and access to labor and supplies, federal, state and local funding, population growth, the need to replace aging infrastructure and commodity prices. The five-year federal surface transportation authorization, which the company says increased highway, bridge and transit funding to its highest level in more than six decades, expired on 2026-09-30 and a short-term extension runs through 2026-12-11, while California's SB-1 funding has no sunset provision. Public work was 78.3% of nine-month 2026 Construction revenue against 71.0% a year earlier, and private Construction revenue fell to USD 749.710 million from USD 786.333 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: The mechanism is that funding lets agencies issue lettings, lettings become awards, and awards become unearned revenue that Granite converts into revenue over about a year; federal lettings are the swing input and state and local measures offset them. The evidence on conversion is mixed: committed and awarded projects grew 6.97% from 2025-12-31 to USD 7,455.470 million, but the third-quarter rise was only USD 36.6 million, and the unearned revenue portion fell from USD 5,056.462 million at 2026-06-30 to USD 4,852.921 million while other awards, which include unexercised options and construction manager general contractor work, rose to USD 2,602.549 million. The credit implication is that near-term revenue is well supported but the 2027 revenue base depends on awards that are not yet contracts. The filing describes public work as approximately 85% of backlog while its own table shows 83.2% at 2026-09-30 and 86.9% at 2025-12-31; this analysis uses the table. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 38, 40–41; calculation calc-06

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Pricing power is limited because contracts are fixed unit price or fixed price. Fixed unit price contracts were 56.9% and fixed price 34.6% of unearned revenue at 2025-12-31, so 91.5% of unearned revenue puts cost increases from inflation, tariffs or inefficiency on Granite unless the contract allows recovery, against 92.3% a year earlier. Customer concentration is low except for the California Department of Transportation at 10.1% of FY2025 revenue, no other customer exceeded 10% in any of the last three years, and the customers are public agencies that award competitively, which gives stability of payment but little room to raise prices. Revenue is therefore predictable and regulated, moderately cyclical through the 16.8% private share of backlog, and exposed to budget decisions rather than to substitution. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation calc-06; calculation calc-07

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The filings do not split fixed from variable costs, but the workforce flexes with the season. Hourly employees ranged from about 2,500 to 5,200 during 2025 against about 2,500 salaried employees, four subsidiaries are party to collective bargaining agreements, and selling, general and administrative expenses were 8.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue, down from 9.3%, so operating leverage worked in Granite's favour as revenue grew and EBITDA margin rose from 8.33% in FY2024 to 11.01% over the last twelve months. The same leverage works in reverse if revenue stalls, because the salaried base and the fixed overhead do not flex at the speed of hourly labor. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-04

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Input costs are the main margin risk. Granite buys aggregates, cement, diesel and gasoline, liquid asphalt, natural gas, propane, resin and steel, and states that fuel and liquid asphalt prices fluctuate with oil, and the filings name tariffs and the conflict in Iran's effect on oil prices as sources of uncertainty. Granite's mitigants are fixed-price forward purchases of oil-related inputs, energy surcharges, schedule adjustments and heating oil derivatives to December 2027, which produced a gain of USD 5.3 million in nine months 2026. The evidence that mitigation is partial is the Materials segment, where energy surcharges offset diesel but cut gross margin from 25.2% to 21.0% in the third quarter; Construction margin rose to 18.6% over the same period, so the cost shock has not shown up in Construction results to date, although how much of the fixed-price backlog is protected by forward purchases is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 39, 41; calculation calc-08

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high and local. Granite competes with firms from small local contractors to national and international groups, some larger than itself, and few compete in all of its markets. Competitors move between the public and private sectors when one is reduced, which the company says can reduce revenue growth or pressure margins; with 83.2% of backlog public, a slowdown in private work would push private competitors into public lettings and could compress bid margins on fixed-price work. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: The threat of new entrants is low in materials and moderate in construction. Aggregate mining and asphalt production need significant capital and face zoning and permitting barriers, so Granite's owned reserves and plants protect its materials margin and supply security, while smaller construction projects need little capital and entry is relatively easy. Larger projects need more capital and bonding, and about USD 4.2 billion of the USD 7.5 billion backlog is bonded through three co-sureties, so surety capacity, which depends on capitalisation and working capital, is a quiet barrier and a dependency. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 48

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Substitution is not a credit issue because aggregates and asphalt are used in nearly all construction and public infrastructure has no practical substitute. Buyer power is high because public agencies award competitively under fixed-price and fixed unit price terms and may modify or cancel contracts, but no customer other than the California Department of Transportation exceeds 10% of revenue, which limits dependence. Supplier power is moderate: the prices of diesel, liquid asphalt, steel and cement and subcontractor capacity are outside Granite's control, vertical integration reduces exposure on aggregates, and subcontractors that cannot obtain surety bonds add performance risk. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 11–12, 14, 18, 20, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41

facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver. Roughly 85% of committed and awarded projects are public work funded from federal, state, regional and local revenues, the federal authorization expired on 2026-09-30 and only a short extension through 2026-12-11 is in place, and Congress is still working on fiscal year 2027 appropriations. The mechanism is that a gap in federal obligations delays lettings, the first effect would be on new awards with timing the filings do not state, and the implication for creditors is a slower revenue base after the current backlog burns off. State and local measures, including California SB-1, offset part of that risk. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39

facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Economic factors are also material. Inflation, tariffs and oil prices drive input costs on fixed-price work, the term loan floats over SOFR with USD 350 million of it swapped to a fixed rate to January 2029, and USD 250 million is unhedged, so interest cost rises with rates on that portion. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the provided materials beyond labor availability, which is covered with cost structure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 38–39; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The main credit supports are scale, visibility and cash conversion. Revenue of USD 5,300.038 million over the last twelve months, an EBITDA margin of 11.01%, free cash flow of USD 443.155 million and net debt of 1.84x EBITDA place Granite at a moderate leverage level, with EBITDA covering cash interest 8.57x and free cash flow earned after that interest, and the replacement of the 3.75% convertible notes with 2034 senior notes showed that the market was open to Granite in June 2026. The constraints are fixed-price risk, integration, a rising interest burden and a structure whose covenants and collateral cannot be assessed from the filings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-04; calculation calc-05

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The trend is toward higher earnings and higher debt. Total debt carrying value rose from USD 739.048 million at the end of 2024 to USD 1,339.129 million at the end of 2025 and USD 1,556.025 million at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA rose from USD 333.694 million to USD 444.879 million and USD 583.582 million, so leverage peaked at 3.11x on 2026-06-30 and is 2.67x now. Cover on cash interest fell from 12.80x in FY2024 to 8.57x. Secured debt is the USD 600.000 million term loan, 1.03x EBITDA, with the revolver undrawn; if the available USD 588.80 million of revolver were fully drawn, secured debt would be USD 1,188.80 million, 2.04x EBITDA, ahead of USD 973.750 million of notes that rank as unsecured on the filings' description (the filings do not state the convertible notes' security), which is the structural point to watch in a downside. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-12; calculation calc-17

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: The short-term outlook for the next 12 to 24 months is supported by backlog and pressured by timing. Tailwinds are the USD 4,852.921 million of unearned revenue, state and local funding including SB-1, higher Construction margins in the third quarter and a USD 140.0 million to USD 160.0 million capital program that is covered by operating cash flow. Headwinds are the end of the federal extension on 2026-12-11, the first coupon on the 2034 senior notes on 2026-12-15, the term loan amortisation from the quarter ending 2026-12-31, the convertible window through 2026-12-31, the weak first and fourth quarters and the diesel and tariff exposure on fixed-price work. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26, 31, 38–41, 46; calculation calc-06; calculation calc-08

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: The medium-term outlook for three to five years turns on reauthorization of federal surface transportation funding, integration of the five acquisitions and the 2029 to 2030 refinancing. The senior notes are callable from 2029-06-15, the interest rate swaps mature in January 2029, the 3.25% convertible notes become freely convertible from 2029-12-15 and mature on 2030-06-15, and the term loan and revolver mature on 2030-08-05, so USD 891.25 million of debt comes due in a seven-month window. The implication is that deleveraging between now and 2029 decides the terms of that refinancing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 25–26, 31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-09

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario is a lapse or long delay in federal reauthorization after 2026-12-11 combined with a diesel or tariff cost shock during the 2027 construction season. The first operating break would be in federal lettings, which would slow new awards while the existing backlog is worked off, and on fixed-price work the cost shock would turn estimate revisions from positive to negative. Illustratively, if EBITDA margin returned to its FY2024 level of 8.33% on last-twelve-month revenue of USD 5,300.038 million, EBITDA would be USD 441.493 million, 24.35% below the current USD 583.582 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17, 38–39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-13

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Granite presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 7.5 billion public-weighted backlog, vertical integration into materials and moderate leverage, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price estimating risk, acquisition integration, a rising cash interest burden and dependence on federal reauthorization. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow has been 68.38% to 75.94% of EBITDA in the periods measured, although part of that rests on billings ahead of revenue. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2029 for the USD 891.25 million falling due in 2030 and on covenant headroom that the filings do not disclose. The primary downside path is a lapse in federal funding combined with a cost shock on fixed-price work, which would cut EBITDA margin while the convertible principal and new coupons call on cash. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indentures, the compliance certificate, the proxy statement, pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses and a peer set, so no comparison with typical leveraged issuers is made. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-05; calculation calc-09; calculation calc-13

Financial foundation for Granite Construction Inc (gva-861459), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied SEC filings, covering FY2024 and FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, with EBITDA calculated because the issuer reports none.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Granite's leverage is moderate at 2.67x total debt and 1.84x net debt to last-twelve-month EBITDA, but total debt has more than doubled since 2024 and cash interest cover has fallen to 8.57x before the new senior notes' coupons begin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–6, 24–31; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–96; calculation calc-15; calculation calc-21

Granite reports no EBITDA, so every multiple uses operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization calculated here, and the non-cash charges from settling the 3.75% convertible notes, which produced a nine-month net loss, sit below operating income and are excluded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 28–30; calculation calc-09

Liquidity is USD 1,069.09 million of cash and undrawn revolver, against USD 381.69 million of debt classified as current, almost all of it the 3.25% convertible notes whose principal holders may require in cash. The credit agreement's covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 26, 30–32, 44–46; calculation calc-19; calculation calc-20
### Evidence, risk and credit analysis

Leverage rose with the acquisition programme and the 2026 refinancing, but earnings grew with it. Debt at carrying value went from USD 739.048 million at the end of 2024 to USD 1,339.129 million at the end of 2025 and USD 1,556.025 million at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA went from USD 333.694 million in FY2024 to USD 444.879 million in FY2025 and USD 583.582 million over the last twelve months, so total debt to EBITDA moved from 2.21x to 3.01x and back to 2.67x. The 2025 step-up came with USD 777.517 million of acquisitions, financed by a USD 600.000 million term loan and cash; 2026 added USD 600.000 million of senior notes due 2034, whose proceeds and cash on hand retired the 3.75% convertible notes with payments of USD 289.7 million in March and USD 714.9 million in August, less capped call proceeds of USD 203.773 million. Net debt therefore rose from USD 160.718 million to USD 1,075.736 million, and net leverage rose from 0.48x to 1.84x, with the 2026-06-30 peak in cash of USD 877.121 million showing how much of the senior notes cash was held before the August settlement.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–96, 139–140; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 24–30; calculation calc-01; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-24

Cash interest cover has fallen and will fall further. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 68.104 million, covered 8.57x by EBITDA against 12.32x for FY2025, but the USD 600.000 million senior notes carry a coupon that adds USD 38.250 million a year with the first payment due on 2026-12-15, the 3.25% convertible notes add their coupon, and the term loan floats over SOFR with USD 350 million swapped to a fixed 3.218% plus margin. No pro forma interest is stated in the filings, so none is calculated; cover on a forward basis is therefore not established. Reported interest expense of USD 329.421 million for nine months is not a cover measure, because USD 273.747 million of it is non-cash discount amortization.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 25, 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation calc-22

Cash-flow quality is good on the face of it but depends on working capital. Operating cash flow was USD 404.270 million for nine months 2026 against USD 89.879 million of capital expenditure, leaving free cash flow of USD 314.391 million, 68.38% of EBITDA. Receivables absorbed USD 325.647 million, offset by USD 192.881 million more payables and a rise in contract liabilities from USD 327.372 million to USD 464.996 million; those billings in excess of revenue are a non-interest-bearing float that would reverse if new awards slowed. The partner share of joint venture cash and the non-controlling distributions also leave the group, so the conversion figure overstates cash available to creditors.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5–6; calculation calc-26

Liquidity covers the near-term claims, with one equity-linked exception. Cash and equivalents were USD 480.289 million, of which USD 149.707 million sits in consolidated joint ventures and is generally not available until distributed, plus USD 588.800 million undrawn on the revolver after USD 11.200 million of letters of credit. Current maturities of USD 381.686 million are almost all the 3.25% convertible notes, which are current because holders may convert through 2026-12-31 while the stock trades above 130% of the USD 77.88 conversion price; principal must be settled in cash on conversion and any premium in cash or shares at the issuer's election. The filing expects no early conversion because the notes trade above conversion value, which is the contrary evidence; it would be overturned if that trading premium disappeared, for example on a fundamental change that let holders put the notes at par or convert with a make-whole adjustment. Surety capacity is a further call on liquidity, with USD 4.2 billion of the USD 7.5 billion backlog bonded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 26, 30–31, 44–48; calculation calc-19

Data and definition risks bound these conclusions. EBITDA is calculated and the credit agreement's own Consolidated EBITDA is not supplied; covenant levels are not printed, so compliance, which the issuer states, cannot be tested. The maturity ladder derives term loan installments from stated percentages. The convertible notes' security is not stated. Lines printed as dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero. Net debt nets all cash, including joint venture cash; excluding it, net leverage would be 2.10x, and netting marketable securities instead would give 1.77x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 30–32, 44–46; calculation calc-25

No event after 2026-09-30 that changes net debt is stated, so no pro forma figure is given. The first-quarter report's subsequent events, the April 2026 acquisition of Kenny Seng Construction for USD 164.1 million and a USD 170.0 million revolver draw, are already in the 2026 interim balance sheets or were repaid in the second quarter. Scheduled calls on cash after the balance sheet date are the first senior notes coupon on 2026-12-15 and the first term loan installment in the quarter ending 2026-12-31, neither of which is an event with a stated net debt effect.

## Gaps

The financial covenant levels in the credit agreement, a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum leverage ratio, and the issuer's reported ratios are not printed in any of the five filings, which state only compliance at each period end. This blocks any covenant headroom measure. Severity: High. The executed credit agreement or a compliance certificate would close it.

The issuer reports no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or reconciliation, so every EBITDA figure is calculated from operating income and depreciation, depletion and amortization and the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA is unknown. This restricts comparison with covenant and market definitions. Severity: Medium. The credit agreement definition would close it.

Carrying values by instrument are not stated, only principal by instrument and one aggregate of issuance costs and other; the 3.25% convertible notes and senior notes are therefore listed at principal. This restricts debt by seniority at carrying value. Severity: Low. The indentures or a detailed debt note would close it.

The term loan's dollar installments are not printed, only the percentage rates, so the maturity ladder applies those rates to the USD 600.000 million initial principal. This restricts the near-year maturity figures. Severity: Medium. The credit agreement schedule would close it.

The security and relative ranking of the 3.25% convertible notes, the guarantor perimeter and any collateral package are not stated beyond the descriptions in the notes. This restricts the debt stack and structural priority work. Severity: Medium. The indentures and guarantee agreements would close it.

Cash interest paid understates the future interest burden because the senior notes issued on 2026-06-02 had paid no coupon by 2026-09-30, and no pro forma interest or current applicable margin is stated. This restricts forward cover. Severity: Medium. The current margin and the swap terms would close it.

Cash includes USD 149.707 million held by consolidated joint ventures that is generally not available until distributed, and the filings do not state how much of the remainder is held in operating subsidiaries or needed for bonding. This restricts the cash netted in net debt and the liquidity figure. Severity: Medium. Management disclosure would close it.

Lines printed as dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero: the debt extinguishment and convertible transaction line for FY2025, nine months 2025 and the third quarter of 2025, the non-cash debt extinguishment and convertible note line for FY2025 and nine months 2025, long-term marketable securities at 2024-12-31, and the conversion derivative liability outside the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. The statements foot without them, so the effect is presentational. Severity: Low.

No balance sheets at the 2025 interim dates and no fiscal 2024 interim reports are supplied, so last-twelve-month leverage starts at 2026-03-31 and the 2025 and 2026 interim cash flow lines exist only for year-to-date periods. Severity: Low. The 2025 quarterly reports would close it.
Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and funds from operations is not stated, so a proxy is used. Severity: Low. Management disclosure would close it.
Segment EBITDA is not stated; segment operating income and depreciation are printed with corporate costs separate. This restricts segment cash flow analysis. Severity: Low.
No event after 2026-09-30 that changes net debt is stated in the sources read; any later financing or acquisition is outside the evidence. Severity: Low.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Granite is a vertically integrated heavy-civil contractor whose public-sector backlog gives creditors good earnings visibility, but five acquisitions since August 2025 and a debt-funded refinancing have made integration and financial policy the credit question. Public customers account for 83.2% of the USD 7.5 billion backlog, and the largest customer was 10.1% of 2025 revenue.

Shareholder cash returns are modest against cash generation, no controlling holder or sponsor is identified, and board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the view of financial policy rests on observed behaviour rather than on documented limits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation calc-05
### Key findings

Revenue visibility is strong but depends on continued public funding. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects of USD 7.5 billion, the largest customer was 10.1% of 2025 revenue, and about USD 3.5 billion of unearned revenue is expected to be recognised within twelve months, so near-term cash flow is largely contracted. The federal highway authorization expired on 2026-09-30 and a short-term extension runs only to 2026-12-11, so the pace of new federal awards is the first thing to watch.

Vertical integration supports cost control and supply but does not insulate every line. Granite owns and leases aggregate reserves and owns processing plants, and Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter from 16.5% a year earlier, but Materials gross margin fell to 21.0% from 25.2% because energy surcharges only offset higher diesel costs, so the materials cushion is thinner than the annual figures suggest.

Fixed-price exposure is large but recent estimate revisions have been favourable. Fixed unit price and fixed price contracts were 91.5% of unearned revenue at the end of 2025, so cost inflation and tariffs fall on Granite unless contracts allow recovery. Nine-month 2026 revisions on projects that each moved profit by USD 5.0 million or more added USD 58.3 million against USD 18.5 million of reductions, which supports estimating quality for now.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation calc-02

Acquisitions are the main change to the credit and integration is unproven. Five deals since August 2025 cost USD 970.9 million in cash; Warren Paving added USD 29.0 million of gross profit on USD 215.1 million of nine-month 2026 revenue, but Papich Construction posted a gross loss of USD 6.3 million, and Kenny Seng Construction earned USD 6.7 million of gross profit on USD 74.8 million of revenue after completion in April 2026. Purchase accounting for the 2026 deals is still preliminary, and the two largest 2025 deals were excluded from the 2025 assessment of internal controls.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 89; calculation calc-01

Financial policy looks measured, but the 2026 convertible settlement shows a willingness to add debt to avoid dilution. Cash dividends and share repurchases in nine months 2026 equal 18.01% of operating cash flow, with USD 121.0 million of repurchase authorisation left. Granite also paid USD 289.7 million in March to exchange USD 100.0 million of convertible principal and USD 714.9 million in August to settle the remaining USD 273.7 million, paying cash plus a small share issuance, funded by USD 600.0 million of senior notes and cash on hand.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 28–30, 49; calculation calc-05

Governance disclosure is thin but shows no creditor-adverse conduct. No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, the chief executive has served since 2021 and the chief financial officer since 2024, and a civil case between the Securities and Exchange Commission and a former officer was resolved in January 2026 with legal costs falling as a result. The auditor has served since 1982 and internal controls were assessed as effective, although the acquired businesses excluded from that assessment were 17.5% of total tangible assets and 4.8% of revenue.

Structure matters for recovery: the term loan and revolver are senior secured, while the senior notes due 2034 are unsecured and guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, so unsecured creditors rank behind secured lenders on any collateral. The collateral package and the guarantor list are not itemised in the filings.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that the acquisition programme has so far coincided with higher margins and a larger backlog: Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter, committed and awarded projects grew 6.97% from the end of 2025 to USD 7.5 billion at 2026-09-30, and shareholder cash returns were only 18.01% of operating cash flow. The view that integration and financial policy are the credit question would be overturned by two further quarters in which Papich Construction returns to a gross profit and Materials margin stabilises. It would be reinforced by another debt-funded acquisition before the term loan begins amortising in the quarter ending 2026-12-31, by repurchases that rise toward free cash flow, or by a lapse in federal highway funding after 2026-12-11.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 13–14, 31, 38, 40–41; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-06
### Limitations

- The proxy statement, which holds board composition, large-holder ownership and executive pay, was not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder or sponsor shapes financial policy is provisional and would change if a large holder with board influence were found.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares or add debt is not established, and the conclusion that financial policy is measured rests on observed behaviour alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 31

- Purchase accounting for the 2026 acquisitions is preliminary and their contributions cover only part-periods, so the conclusion that integration is unproven could move either way as the measurement periods close.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10
- Segment EBITDA is not stated, so margin conclusions use gross profit and operating income, and a shift of corporate costs between segments would change the comparison of Construction and Materials.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36

- The backlog includes unexercised options and awards that customers may cancel or modify, so the revenue-visibility conclusion is weaker for the portion that is not unearned revenue on executed contracts.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Granite completed five acquisitions for USD 970.9 million in cash between August 2025 and September 2026: Warren Paving for USD 540.0 million and Papich Construction for USD 170.0 million on 2025-08-05, Cinderlite for USD 58.5 million on 2025-10-03, Kenny Seng Construction for USD 164.1 million on 2026-04-23, and the remaining half of an asphalt terminal entity for USD 38.3 million on 2026-09-09. The deals extend vertically integrated home markets in the Southeast, California's Central Coast and Central Valley, Nevada and Utah, and add property and equipment, mineral reserves and goodwill to the balance sheet.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65, 118–121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–15; calculation calc-01

Financing changed in two steps. On 2025-08-05 Granite entered a senior secured credit agreement with a USD 600.0 million revolver, a USD 600.0 million term loan and a USD 75.0 million delayed draw term loan, which, with a USD 10.0 million revolver draw and cash on hand, funded the 2025 acquisitions. In 2026 it issued USD 600.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2034 on 2026-06-02 and used the proceeds, cash on hand and capped call unwind proceeds to exchange and then settle all of the 3.75% convertible notes, leaving the 3.25% convertible notes of USD 373.75 million due 2030 and the term loan as the other debt.
New debt is therefore secured bank debt plus unsecured notes, and part of the 2026 issue replaced equity-linked instruments rather than adding to total debt at the same pace.

## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Granite Construction Inc (gva-861459), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business quality, financial profile, downside path and monitoring triggers, drawn from the five supplied SEC filings and the earlier module outputs, with no rating, recovery or position-sizing conclusion.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Granite's credit profile is adequate: contracted public backlog, moderate leverage and USD 1,069.09 million of liquidity cover near-term claims, but five acquisitions and a rising interest burden leave limited room for a margin or funding shock.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-01

Public customers are 83.2% of the backlog and fixed-price contracts were 91.5% of unearned revenue at the end of 2025, so a funding pause or cost overrun reaches EBITDA directly. Net debt is 1.84x last-twelve-month EBITDA, but cash interest cover of 8.57x does not yet include coupons on the 2034 senior notes, and USD 373.75 million of 3.25% convertible principal is cash-settled if holders convert.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 40; calculation calc-03; calculation calc-06; calculation calc-07
### Key findings

Revenue durability is the main credit support, with a funding date to watch. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects of USD 7.5 billion at 2026-09-30, and about USD 3.5 billion of unearned revenue is expected within twelve months, so near-term revenue is contracted. Backlog rose only 0.5% in the third quarter and unearned revenue fell 4.03% as other awards rose, and the federal highway extension ends on 2026-12-11, so the conversion of awards into executed contracts and the pace of federal lettings are the items to watch.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 38, 40–41; calculation calc-06

Margins are improving but exposed to cost inflation. Construction gross margin rose to 18.6% in the third quarter from 16.5% a year earlier and last-twelve-month EBITDA margin is 11.01% against 10.06% in FY2025, but Materials gross margin fell to 21.0% from 25.2% because, as the company explains, energy surcharges that offset elevated diesel costs lower the margin, and fixed-price contracts were 91.5% of unearned revenue, so a diesel, tariff or labor shock would reduce EBITDA before it reduced revenue.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation calc-04; calculation calc-07; calculation calc-08

Cash conversion is good but leans on working capital. Free cash flow was 68.38% of EBITDA in nine months 2026 and 74.32% in FY2025, and contract liabilities rose by USD 137.62 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, a float that would reverse if awards slowed, so conversion supports debt service only while the backlog keeps growing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-05; calculation calc-14

Leverage is moderate but has risen and interest cover has fallen. Total debt is 2.67x and net debt 1.84x last-twelve-month EBITDA against 3.01x and 1.82x at the end of 2025, total debt is 2.11x its end-2024 level, and cash interest cover is 8.57x against 12.32x for FY2025 before any coupon on the 2034 senior notes, so a drop in EBITDA moves cover faster than leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03

Liquidity covers near-term claims but not all of it is free. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,069.09 million is 2.80x the USD 381.69 million of debt classified as current, almost all of it the 3.25% convertible notes, and USD 149.71 million of the cash sits in consolidated joint ventures that Granite cannot freely use, so the cushion is smaller than the headline.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 45–46; calculation calc-01; calculation calc-02

Refinancing capacity looks adequate but rests on market access before 2030. The 2034 senior notes were placed in June 2026 and carried a fair value of 96.65% of principal at 2026-09-30, and the term loan and revolver mature on 2030-08-05, so USD 891.25 million falls due in 2030 once the convertible notes are included and the maturity wall is a 2029 refinancing task, not a 2026 or 2027 one.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 24–31; calculation calc-09; calculation calc-10

Financial policy is the swing factor, not sponsor behaviour. No controlling holder is identified and shareholder cash returns were 18.01% of operating cash flow, but the 2026 cash settlement of the 3.75% convertible notes and ongoing repurchases show that leverage tolerance rose with acquisitions, so a further debt-funded deal or larger buybacks would be the first sign of weaker creditor alignment.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–30, 49; calculation calc-11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is that earnings and cash flow have grown faster than debt since the end of 2025: last-twelve-month EBITDA is 31.18% above FY2025 while total debt is 16.20% higher, EBITDA grew 43.20% in nine months 2026, last-twelve-month free cash flow was 0.28x total debt, backlog grew 6.97% since year-end, and net debt to EBITDA of 1.84x is below the 2.10x of 2026-03-31. The adequate view would strengthen with two quarters of free cash flow above 50% of EBITDA, a stable Materials margin, no further debt-funded acquisition and a federal reauthorization before 2026-12-11. It would weaken with a revolver draw to fund operations, cash conversion below 50% of EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA above the 3.11x of 2026-06-30, or conversion of the 3.25% convertible notes before the 2030 refinancing is arranged.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 40; calculation calc-03; calculation calc-04; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-06
### Limitations

- Covenant levels are not printed, so the conclusion that leverage and liquidity leave adequate room is judged against observed ranges and not against headroom, which could be tighter than the ratios suggest.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

- No ratings, market spreads or peer set were supplied, so the conclusion that the profile is adequate rests on general experience of contractors of this size and could rank differently against named peers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- The forward interest burden is not stated, so the conclusion that cover is falling rests on cash paid to date, and a full year of coupons on the 2034 senior notes would lower it further.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 30
- Acquired businesses contribute for part periods, so the conclusion that margins are improving may reflect mix and timing as much as underlying execution.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–15
- The downside path is qualitative with one illustrative sensitivity, so the conclusion that Granite avoids liquidity distress in it depends on management actions the filings do not commit to.
Basis: calculation calc-13
### Source gate and module status

Module status: Ready with Limitations. The five filings, covering FY2024, FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, and the earlier outputs on source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance are all available and agree on entity, period and currency (Granite Construction Incorporated, consolidated, USD). The datapoints taken from Business & governance are the committed and awarded projects of USD 7,455.470 million, the contract mix at 2025-12-31 and the behaviour flags for 2026. ### Company description and credit linkage

Granite is a vertically integrated US civil contractor and construction materials producer, listed on the New York Stock Exchange and headquartered in Watsonville, California. The Construction segment, 83.4% of nine-month 2026 revenue, builds highways, bridges, rail, water, power and defence-related projects, predominantly for federal, state and local agencies. The Materials segment mines aggregates and makes asphalt, partly for Granite's own projects and partly for third parties. Revenue was USD 4,424.379 million in FY2025 and USD 5,300.038 million over the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, a rise of 19.79% that includes five acquisitions since August 2025 for USD 970.9 million in cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36, 38; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-15

The credit link is visibility with an execution tail. Public customers are 83.2% of committed and awarded projects, the largest customer, the California Department of Transportation, was 10.1% of FY2025 revenue after 14.2% in FY2024, and unearned revenue on executed contracts is USD 4,852.921 million, of which about USD 3.5 billion is expected within twelve months, equal to 66.04% of last-twelve-month revenue, so creditors can see about two-thirds of a year's revenue and the rest must come from awards not yet in unearned revenue and from short-cycle work. Pricing is mostly fixed, however, so cash-generation durability depends on estimating and cost control rather than on contractual pass-through, and the debt-funded acquisitions have added integration risk to a business whose reported EBITDA has to be calculated because Granite states none.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 40; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-06; calculation calc-07; calculation calc-16
### Ownership and group structure

Granite is a listed Delaware corporation with 44,130,293 shares outstanding at 2026-10-23. No controlling holder, sponsor or parent is identified in the filings, and board composition, large-holder percentages and executive pay sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the absence of a controlling owner is an observation of what the filings do not say and not a tested finding. The chief executive has served since June 2021, the chief financial officer since September 2024, and the chief executive became sole chief operating decision maker when the chief operating officer retired on 2025-07-04, which concentrates top-level decisions at a time of integration.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 21–22; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The group structure matters for creditors. The borrowers under the credit agreement are Granite Construction Incorporated, Granite Construction Company and GILC Incorporated, the senior notes due 2034 are unsecured and guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under that agreement, and the convertible notes are issued by the parent with no stated guarantee or collateral. Consolidated construction joint ventures, ten active projects with Granite's share between 50.0% and 70.0%, hold USD 149.707 million of cash, of which Granite's own portion is USD 93.3 million, that is generally not available until distributed and carry joint and several performance obligations, so part of the reported cash and backlog belongs to partners. The collateral package, guarantor list and restricted payment capacity are not itemised, so the ranking of unsecured creditors behind the USD 600.000 million secured term loan is a description of the filings and not a legal conclusion.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22, 25, 30–31, 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial policy shows moderate tolerance for leverage and modest shareholder distributions. Dividends of USD 0.13 per share a quarter together with repurchases of USD 55.772 million in nine months 2026 took 18.01% of operating cash flow, USD 121.0 million of the 2022 repurchase authorisation remains, and Granite settled the 3.75% convertible notes largely in cash, funded by new senior notes and cash on hand. Creditors are not worse off for that choice in the filings read, since no priming, uptier or drop-down is described, but the choice increased cash claims ahead of equity and shows that management will use debt capacity when it sees value.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 28–30, 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-11
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is project-based, backlog-supported and public-funding-driven. The five economic drivers Granite names are the health of the US economy and access to labor and supplies, federal, state and local funding, population growth, the need to replace aging infrastructure and commodity prices. The five-year federal surface transportation authorization, which the company says increased highway, bridge and transit funding to its highest level in more than six decades, expired on 2026-09-30 and a short-term extension runs through 2026-12-11, while California's SB-1 funding has no sunset provision. Public work was 78.3% of nine-month 2026 Construction revenue against 71.0% a year earlier, and private Construction revenue fell to USD 749.710 million from USD 786.333 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40

The mechanism is that funding lets agencies issue lettings, lettings become awards, and awards become unearned revenue that Granite converts into revenue over about a year; federal lettings are the swing input and state and local measures offset them. The evidence on conversion is mixed: committed and awarded projects grew 6.97% from 2025-12-31 to USD 7,455.470 million, but the third-quarter rise was only USD 36.6 million, and the unearned revenue portion fell from USD 5,056.462 million at 2026-06-30 to USD 4,852.921 million while other awards, which include unexercised options and construction manager general contractor work, rose to USD 2,602.549 million. The credit implication is that near-term revenue is well supported but the 2027 revenue base depends on awards that are not yet contracts. The filing describes public work as approximately 85% of backlog while its own table shows 83.2% at 2026-09-30 and 86.9% at 2025-12-31; this analysis uses the table.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 38, 40–41; calculation calc-06

Pricing power is limited because contracts are fixed unit price or fixed price. Fixed unit price contracts were 56.9% and fixed price 34.6% of unearned revenue at 2025-12-31, so 91.5% of unearned revenue puts cost increases from inflation, tariffs or inefficiency on Granite unless the contract allows recovery, against 92.3% a year earlier. Customer concentration is low except for the California Department of Transportation at 10.1% of FY2025 revenue, no other customer exceeded 10% in any of the last three years, and the customers are public agencies that award competitively, which gives stability of payment but little room to raise prices. Revenue is therefore predictable and regulated, moderately cyclical through the 16.8% private share of backlog, and exposed to budget decisions rather than to substitution.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation calc-06; calculation calc-07
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The filings do not split fixed from variable costs, but the workforce flexes with the season. Hourly employees ranged from about 2,500 to 5,200 during 2025 against about 2,500 salaried employees, four subsidiaries are party to collective bargaining agreements, and selling, general and administrative expenses were 8.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue, down from 9.3%, so operating leverage worked in Granite's favour as revenue grew and EBITDA margin rose from 8.33% in FY2024 to 11.01% over the last twelve months. The same leverage works in reverse if revenue stalls, because the salaried base and the fixed overhead do not flex at the speed of hourly labor.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-04

Input costs are the main margin risk. Granite buys aggregates, cement, diesel and gasoline, liquid asphalt, natural gas, propane, resin and steel, and states that fuel and liquid asphalt prices fluctuate with oil, and the filings name tariffs and the conflict in Iran's effect on oil prices as sources of uncertainty. Granite's mitigants are fixed-price forward purchases of oil-related inputs, energy surcharges, schedule adjustments and heating oil derivatives to December 2027, which produced a gain of USD 5.3 million in nine months 2026. The evidence that mitigation is partial is the Materials segment, where energy surcharges offset diesel but cut gross margin from 25.2% to 21.0% in the third quarter; Construction margin rose to 18.6% over the same period, so the cost shock has not shown up in Construction results to date, although how much of the fixed-price backlog is protected by forward purchases is not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 39, 41; calculation calc-08

Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a combined cost and volume shock, which is an analyst judgement from the cost structure above. Estimate revisions on larger projects added USD 58.3 million against USD 18.5 million of reductions in nine months 2026, which supports estimating quality, and Papich Construction's gross loss of USD 6.3 million shows that acquired businesses can still reverse that. Integration costs are small to date, with other costs, net of USD 15.441 million against USD 38.698 million a year earlier.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13–17, 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is moderate. Purchases of property and equipment were USD 138.270 million in FY2025, 3.13% of revenue, and USD 89.879 million in nine months 2026, 2.17% of revenue, and 2026 guidance is USD 140.0 million to USD 160.0 million including about USD 50.0 million of strategic materials investment. The company says the timing and amount of capital expenditure can vary with project progress and business outlook, so there is some flexibility over the maturity wall, but the maintenance and growth split is not stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-15

Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 330.646 million in FY2025 and USD 443.155 million over the last twelve months, 74.32% and 75.94% of EBITDA, and USD 314.391 million in nine months 2026, 68.38%. The sources of that cash matter. Operating cash flow of USD 404.270 million in nine months 2026 was helped by USD 192.881 million more payables and by a rise in contract liabilities from USD 327.372 million to USD 464.996 million, while receivables absorbed USD 325.647 million, so working capital timing both flatters and depresses conversion from quarter to quarter. Lease liabilities of USD 191.510 million are outside the debt figure, distributions to joint venture partners were USD 13.248 million in nine months 2026, and the first and fourth quarters are seasonally weakest, so cash flow is uneven within the year even when the full year converts well.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5–6, 24, 39; calculation calc-05; calculation calc-14

EBITDA has translated into free cash flow, after cash interest and capital expenditure, of 68.38% to 75.94% of EBITDA in each period measured, which covers the scheduled term loan installments of USD 3.750 million in FY2026 and USD 18.750 million in FY2027 many times over. The test is the next 24 months, when the first coupon on the 2034 senior notes falls due on 2026-12-15, the term loan begins to amortise in the quarter ending 2026-12-31, and a working capital reversal would reduce the float on which part of the conversion rests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-05; calculation calc-12
### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is high and local. Granite competes with firms from small local contractors to national and international groups, some larger than itself, and few compete in all of its markets. Competitors move between the public and private sectors when one is reduced, which the company says can reduce revenue growth or pressure margins; with 83.2% of backlog public, a slowdown in private work would push private competitors into public lettings and could compress bid margins on fixed-price work.

The threat of new entrants is low in materials and moderate in construction. Aggregate mining and asphalt production need significant capital and face zoning and permitting barriers, so Granite's owned reserves and plants protect its materials margin and supply security, while smaller construction projects need little capital and entry is relatively easy. Larger projects need more capital and bonding, and about USD 4.2 billion of the USD 7.5 billion backlog is bonded through three co-sureties, so surety capacity, which depends on capitalisation and working capital, is a quiet barrier and a dependency.

Substitution is not a credit issue because aggregates and asphalt are used in nearly all construction and public infrastructure has no practical substitute. Buyer power is high because public agencies award competitively under fixed-price and fixed unit price terms and may modify or cancel contracts, but no customer other than the California Department of Transportation exceeds 10% of revenue, which limits dependence. Supplier power is moderate: the prices of diesel, liquid asphalt, steel and cement and subcontractor capacity are outside Granite's control, vertical integration reduces exposure on aggregates, and subcontractors that cannot obtain surety bonds add performance risk.
### Macro and policy factors

Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver. Roughly 85% of committed and awarded projects are public work funded from federal, state, regional and local revenues, the federal authorization expired on 2026-09-30 and only a short extension through 2026-12-11 is in place, and Congress is still working on fiscal year 2027 appropriations. The mechanism is that a gap in federal obligations delays lettings, the first effect would be on new awards with timing the filings do not state, and the implication for creditors is a slower revenue base after the current backlog burns off. State and local measures, including California SB-1, offset part of that risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39

Economic factors are also material. Inflation, tariffs and oil prices drive input costs on fixed-price work, the term loan floats over SOFR with USD 350 million of it swapped to a fixed rate to January 2029, and USD 250 million is unhedged, so interest cost rises with rates on that portion. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the provided materials beyond labor availability, which is covered with cost structure.

Strengths:

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation calc-06
- Vertical integration protects supply. Owned aggregate reserves and plants give a materials margin outside contracting and secure inputs for Construction.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-01; calculation calc-02

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-05; calculation calc-09
Weaknesses:
- Fixed-price exposure. 91.5% of unearned revenue is fixed unit price or fixed price, so cost inflation falls on Granite.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation calc-07
- Acquisition integration. Five deals cost USD 970.9 million, purchase accounting for the 2026 deals is preliminary, and Papich Construction posted a gross loss.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-15
