- Opaque structure. The collateral, guarantor list and restricted payment capacity are not itemised.

Opportunities: continued state and local funding and IIJA-funded lettings could extend backlog growth, the USD 50.0 million of strategic materials investment may expand materials supply and margin, and a longer-term federal reauthorization would restore multi-year visibility; each would improve revenue visibility and margin durability.

Threats: a lapse in federal funding after 2026-12-11, a diesel or tariff shock on fixed-price work, conversion of the 3.25% convertible notes before refinancing, and surety capacity constraints on a large bonded backlog; each would reduce earnings or liquidity.
### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are scale, visibility and cash conversion. Revenue of USD 5,300.038 million over the last twelve months, an EBITDA margin of 11.01%, free cash flow of USD 443.155 million and net debt of 1.84x EBITDA place Granite at a moderate leverage level, with EBITDA covering cash interest 8.57x and free cash flow earned after that interest, and the replacement of the 3.75% convertible notes with 2034 senior notes showed that the market was open to Granite in June 2026. The constraints are fixed-price risk, integration, a rising interest burden and a structure whose covenants and collateral cannot be assessed from the filings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-04; calculation calc-05

The trend is toward higher earnings and higher debt. Total debt carrying value rose from USD 739.048 million at the end of 2024 to USD 1,339.129 million at the end of 2025 and USD 1,556.025 million at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA rose from USD 333.694 million to USD 444.879 million and USD 583.582 million, so leverage peaked at 3.11x on 2026-06-30 and is 2.67x now. Cover on cash interest fell from 12.80x in FY2024 to 8.57x. Secured debt is the USD 600.000 million term loan, 1.03x EBITDA, with the revolver undrawn; if the available USD 588.80 million of revolver were fully drawn, secured debt would be USD 1,188.80 million, 2.04x EBITDA, ahead of USD 973.750 million of notes that rank as unsecured on the filings' description (the filings do not state the convertible notes' security), which is the structural point to watch in a downside.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-12; calculation calc-17

Key datapoints missing for a more definitive view are the covenant levels and compliance certificate, the indentures and credit agreement, the proxy statement, pro forma EBITDA for acquired businesses, the current term loan margin and a peer set or ratings.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The short-term outlook for the next 12 to 24 months is supported by backlog and pressured by timing. Tailwinds are the USD 4,852.921 million of unearned revenue, state and local funding including SB-1, higher Construction margins in the third quarter and a USD 140.0 million to USD 160.0 million capital program that is covered by operating cash flow. Headwinds are the end of the federal extension on 2026-12-11, the first coupon on the 2034 senior notes on 2026-12-15, the term loan amortisation from the quarter ending 2026-12-31, the convertible window through 2026-12-31, the weak first and fourth quarters and the diesel and tariff exposure on fixed-price work.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26, 31, 38–41, 46; calculation calc-06; calculation calc-08

The medium-term outlook for three to five years turns on reauthorization of federal surface transportation funding, integration of the five acquisitions and the 2029 to 2030 refinancing. The senior notes are callable from 2029-06-15, the interest rate swaps mature in January 2029, the 3.25% convertible notes become freely convertible from 2029-12-15 and mature on 2030-06-15, and the term loan and revolver mature on 2030-08-05, so USD 891.25 million of debt comes due in a seven-month window. The implication is that deleveraging between now and 2029 decides the terms of that refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 25–26, 31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-09
### Downside scenario

The scenario is a lapse or long delay in federal reauthorization after 2026-12-11 combined with a diesel or tariff cost shock during the 2027 construction season. The first operating break would be in federal lettings, which would slow new awards while the existing backlog is worked off, and on fixed-price work the cost shock would turn estimate revisions from positive to negative. Illustratively, if EBITDA margin returned to its FY2024 level of 8.33% on last-twelve-month revenue of USD 5,300.038 million, EBITDA would be USD 441.493 million, 24.35% below the current USD 583.582 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17, 38–39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-13

The financial transmission is manageable but not trivial. On that EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA would be 3.52x and net debt to EBITDA 2.44x, cover would be 6.48x on last-twelve-month cash interest and 4.15x if a full year of the senior notes coupon of USD 38.250 million is added as a rough allowance (Financial foundation states no pro forma interest, and this is analyst arithmetic on the stated rate and principal), and free cash flow would fall to about USD 301.066 million before any tax offset, to USD 163.442 million if the USD 137.624 million contract liability float reversed, and to USD 125.192 million after the senior notes coupon. Liquidity of USD 1,069.089 million would be USD 695.339 million if all USD 373.750 million of the convertible principal were paid in cash, though a falling share price would also remove the share-price condition that currently lets holders convert and so the early call on cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation calc-12; calculation calc-13; calculation calc-14

Management levers are repurchases of USD 55.772 million in nine months 2026, the timing of the USD 50.0 million strategic materials program, acquisition spending and seasonal labor. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario because free cash flow stays positive and liquidity exceeds the convertible principal, but headroom against covenants is not established, and the secured revolver is the instrument that would absorb any shortfall ahead of the unsecured notes. Default is not the base case and the filings give no evidence for it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 31, 46, 49; calculation calc-13; calculation calc-17
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths, in rank order:

- Public backlog visibility. Unearned revenue of USD 4,852.921 million on executed contracts and a public share of 83.2% of backlog mean about two-thirds of a year's revenue is under executed contracts, mostly with public agencies, which protects debt service while awards are pending.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 40; calculation calc-06
- Liquidity above near-term claims. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 1,069.089 million are 2.80x debt classified as current, so the convertible principal can be paid without new funding.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-01; calculation calc-02

- Vertical integration. Owned aggregate reserves and plants secure inputs and give Granite a materials margin outside contracting, which reduces supplier power and shortens the route from cost inflation to margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12
- Cash conversion. Free cash flow of 68.38% of EBITDA in nine months 2026 funds capital expenditure and debt service internally, though it leans on billing ahead of revenue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-05; calculation calc-14
- Moderate leverage with earnings growth. Net debt of 1.84x EBITDA, with EBITDA up 43.20% in nine months, leaves room to absorb a margin dip before cover becomes a concern.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-04
Weaknesses, in rank order:

- Fixed-price cost exposure. 91.5% of unearned revenue is fixed unit price or fixed price, so inflation, tariffs or overruns reduce margin before revenue and are the likeliest route to higher leverage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation calc-07

- Acquisition integration and debt-funded growth. Five deals cost USD 970.9 million, purchase accounting is preliminary and Papich Construction posted a gross loss, so integration failure would cut EBITDA on a larger debt base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-15
- Rising cash interest burden. Cover fell from 12.32x to 8.57x before any coupon on the 2034 senior notes, so a margin dip lowers cover faster than it raises leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-03; calculation calc-12
- Federal funding dependence. Public work is 83.2% of backlog and the federal extension ends on 2026-12-11, so a lapse would slow new awards.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 40
- Opaque covenants and structure. Covenant levels, collateral and the guarantor list are not printed, so headroom and the position of unsecured notes behind the secured loan cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gva-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 30–32; calculation calc-17

### Overall credit view

Overall, Granite presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 7.5 billion public-weighted backlog, vertical integration into materials and moderate leverage, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price estimating risk, acquisition integration, a rising cash interest burden and dependence on federal reauthorization. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow has been 68.38% to 75.94% of EBITDA in the periods measured, although part of that rests on billings ahead of revenue. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2029 for the USD 891.25 million falling due in 2030 and on covenant headroom that the filings do not disclose. The primary downside path is a lapse in federal funding combined with a cost shock on fixed-price work, which would cut EBITDA margin while the convertible principal and new coupons call on cash. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indentures, the compliance certificate, the proxy statement, pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses and a peer set, so no comparison with typical leveraged issuers is made.
